messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: The institutional foundations that held this regime together are visibly crumbling.
ATMOSPHERE: The fear barrier has collapsed. People who were terrified last week are now openly discussing action.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] sharp blame-shifting and reversing decisions within hours among leadership
  - [Security Forces] This is hard to escape the conclusion that past the point of concealment — an informant in the security services says internal surveillance has shifted from opposition to other security units
  - [Money And Logistics] insurance premiums for commercial properties in the capital have spiked without public explanation (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Street Mood] street talk has shifted from complaint to anticipation — people speak as if change is imaginable — the trend decelerating and losing whatever energy it had
  - [Information Control] internet speeds have been throttled in the capital without official acknowledgment
  - [Personal Observations] your superior at work has been evasive and cancelled two meetings without rescheduling — the trend decelerating and losing whatever energy it had
  - [Diplomatic Signals] an international NGO that normally coordinates with the government has begun operating independently (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] emergency services responded to a recent incident with visible disorganization — the coordination mechanisms are fraying — the trend decelerating and losing whatever energy it had

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - Whether the security apparatus would follow orders to suppress a large-scale mobilization, or stand aside.
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think it's time to be prepared for anything - the regime's grip is weakening fast, and people are starting to sense it. I've seen it in the way people are talking, and even some of those in power seem to be losing their nerve, but we still need to be careful, for our own sake.
